# NTP

`c.NTP` calls the API's NTP group. The NTP servers of chrony, and its sync
status.

## Methods

| Method                                    | Returns                            | Permission  | Description                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| [`Get(ctx, hostname)`](#get)              | `*Response[Collection[NtpStatus]]` | `ntp:read`  | Get the sync status of chrony and its sources. |
| [`Create(ctx, hostname, input)`](#create) | `*Response[Collection[NtpResult]]` | `ntp:write` | Set the NTP servers that chrony uses.          |
| [`Update(ctx, hostname, input)`](#update) | `*Response[Collection[NtpResult]]` | `ntp:write` | Replace the NTP servers that osapi set.        |
| [`Delete(ctx, hostname)`](#delete)        | `*Response[Collection[NtpResult]]` | `ntp:write` | Remove the NTP servers that osapi set.         |

### Get

```go
func (s *NTPService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[NtpStatus]], error)
```

Get the sync status of chrony and its sources.

Reads chronyc tracking, for whether chrony is synchronized, its stratum, its
offset from NTP time and the source that it follows, and chronyc sources, for
each source that it has.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/ntp`, and needs the permission `ntp:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A host synchronized to time.cloudflare.com, `go run ntp.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Get(ctx, target)
```

### Create

```go
func (s *NTPService) Create(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input NTPCreateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[NtpResult]], error)
```

Set the NTP servers that chrony uses.

Writes a server line for each server to /etc/chrony/sources.d/osapi-ntp.sources,
and reloads the sources with chronyc reload sources. A file that has the same
servers does not change, and reports changed: false.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/ntp`, and needs the permission `ntp:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Set two servers, `go run ntp.go create`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Create(ctx, target, client.NTPCreateInput{Servers: []string{"0.pool.ntp.org", "1.pool.ntp.org"}})
```

The servers that the host has, `go run ntp.go create-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Create(ctx, target, client.NTPCreateInput{Servers: []string{"0.pool.ntp.org"}})
```

### Update

```go
func (s *NTPService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input NTPUpdateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[NtpResult]], error)
```

Replace the NTP servers that osapi set.

The same as create, for servers that osapi set already. It fails with not found
when osapi set none. The servers that the file has already report changed:
false.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/ntp`, and needs the permission `ntp:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Replace the servers, `go run ntp.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Update(ctx, target, client.NTPUpdateInput{Servers: []string{"time.cloudflare.com"}})
```

The servers that the file has, `go run ntp.go update-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Update(ctx, target, client.NTPUpdateInput{Servers: []string{"0.pool.ntp.org"}})
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *NTPService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[NtpResult]], error)
```

Remove the NTP servers that osapi set.

Removes /etc/chrony/sources.d/osapi-ntp.sources and reloads the sources, so
chrony uses its other sources. When osapi set no servers, it reports changed:
false.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/ntp`, and needs the permission
`ntp:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove the servers, `go run ntp.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.NTP.Delete(ctx, target)
```

### RowStatus

What happened on the host: ok, the operation ran and succeeded; failed, it ran
and did not succeed; skipped, the host's OS family does not support it; timeout,
the host did not answer, so nobody knows whether it ran.

A `string`, one of `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`, `timeout`.
